Note::is_scalar¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::is_scalar() const noexcept

Test For Rank Zero¶

is_scalar() is true only for a defined rank-zero Note. It describes geometry, not cardinality: a vector with shape [1] contains one cell but is not scalar. That distinction determines whether indexing requires zero or one coordinates and whether shape-preserving operations return [] or [1].

An undefined handle reports false even though its non-throwing dim() fallback is zero. Empty text does not affect the result. The query is constant-time, allocation-free, and noexcept.

Example 1: Scalar Versus Singleton Vector¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make("alpha");
const auto singleton = pluss::note::make({"alpha"});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar: " << scalar.is_scalar() << " sizes=" << scalar.sizes().size() << '\n'
          << "singleton: " << singleton.is_scalar() << " dim=" << singleton.dim() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar: true sizes=0
singleton: false dim=1

Example 2: Empty Text Remains Scalar¶

const auto value = pluss::note::make("");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar=" << value.is_scalar()
          << " empty=" << value.empty()
          << " bytes=" << value.lengths_bytes()[0] << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=true empty=false bytes=0

Example 3: Undefined Is Not Scalar¶

const auto value = pluss::Note::undefined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << value.defined()
          << " dim=" << value.dim()
          << " scalar=" << value.is_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=false dim=0 scalar=false
